items.t: El Al Israel Airlines (TASE:ELAL) Climbed, But What Is Drawing Attention Now?
sum: El Al Israel Airlines (TASE:ELAL) just posted third quarter 2026 results that paired higher sales with lower profit, a mix that gives you a clear snapshot of the trade off between growth and earnings.

That mixed earnings picture came at a time when momentum has been rebuilding in El Al Israel Airlines shares. The 30 day share price return was 8.77% and the 90 day gain was 19.58%. These contributed to a 1 year total shareholder return of 32.95% and a very large 5 year total shareholder return, all based on a latest share price of ₪19.48.

After a run to ₪19.48 on mixed earnings, the real tension around El Al Israel Airlines now sits in the gap between that price and fair value estimates. How wide is that spread, and which side does the risk lean toward?
Preferred P/E of 11.8x for El Al Israel Airlines: Is it justified?
On valuation, the spotlight falls on earnings. El Al Israel Airlines trades on a P/E of 11.8x, while our DCF model points to a future cash flow value of ₪6.45 against the current ₪19.48 share price.

The P/E multiple tells you how much investors are paying for each unit of net profit. In this case, the market is valuing El Al Israel Airlines at 11.8 times its earnings, which sits above the peer average of 7.2x and below the broader Asian Airlines industry at 14.1x.

That mix sends a split signal. Compared with direct peers, the stock looks expensive, which suggests the market is willing to pay more for its current earnings profile. Against the wider Asian Airlines group, the same P/E appears more restrained, which could imply investors are pricing in a more conservative outlook than the broader regional sector.
